calculate_iban.description: Build an IBAN from a country, a bank code and an account number, the conversion a record still holding a German Bankleitzahl and Kontonummer needs before it can be paid by SEPA transfer. openiban validates whatever it builds, so the answer carries the same checks a validation would, plus the bank's name and BIC where it has them. No API key required.
calculate_iban.display_str_template: Calculate the {0} IBAN for account {2} at bank {1}.
calculate_iban.name: calculate_iban

parameters.description: The country the account is held in. The list comes from openiban's own country map; the seven countries it holds bank data for are listed first.
parameters.name: country_code

parameters.description: The bank's domestic code: a German Bankleitzahl (37040044), a Dutch bank's four letters (ABNA), a Swiss clearing number. Spaces are ignored.
parameters.name: bank_code

parameters.description: The domestic account number, exactly as the bank writes it, leading zeros included. Spaces are ignored.
parameters.name: account_number

parameters.description: Also check the bank code and return the bank's name, BIC, city and postcode alongside the IBAN. On by default. Turning it off uses openiban's smaller calculate endpoint, which returns the IBAN alone and does not check that the bank code exists.
parameters.name: look_up_bank

returns.description: One calculated IBAN and everything openiban reports about it.

calculate_ibans.description: Build IBANs for a whole list of accounts in one country, in one step: the migration action for a customer or payroll table that still holds bank codes and account numbers. No API key required.

get_country.description: Look one country up by name or by code, and get back the two-letter code an IBAN from there starts with. Use it when the country arrives as a name from somewhere else in the workflow, a CRM field saying 'Germany', and the next step needs 'DE'. It also says whether openiban holds bank data there. No API key required.
get_country.name: get_country

parameters.description: The country to look up. Pick one from the list, or type a value coming from an earlier step: a name ('Germany'), a code ('DE'), or part of a name ('Nether' finds the Netherlands). A name is matched first, then a code.
parameters.name: country

bank_data_available.description: Whether openiban holds bank codes and BICs for this country.

code.description: The two-letter country code, ready to hand to the calculate actions.

code_is_shared.description: True when openiban files more than one name under this code, which it does for France's 'FR' and the United Kingdom's 'GB'. The code is still the right one to hand to the calculate actions.

bank_data_available.description: Whether openiban holds bank codes and BICs for this country, so a validation there comes back with the bank's name and BIC.

validate_iban.description: Check that an IBAN is a real one before you pay it: the check digits, the country's own length rule, and whether the bank code inside it exists. Where openiban holds bank data it also returns the bank's name and BIC, so one step both validates the account and tells you who it belongs to. No API key required.

description: Validate IBANs and look up the bank behind them. Check one IBAN or a whole payment file at once (the check digits, the country's length rule and whether the bank code really exists) and get back the bank's name and BIC (SWIFT code) for Austria, Belgium, Germany, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Switzerland. Build IBANs from a bank code and an account number to migrate records that still hold domestic account details, and list the countries and country codes the service knows. No account or API key required.
